paper.title: Tight (Lower) Bounds for the Fixed Budget Best Arm Identification Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Best arm identification with fixed budget, distributions on [0,1] (lower bound)
unmapped: Lower bound holds over the class B_a of problems with complexity H <= a; the learner may know the upper bound a on H
settings.definition_quote: Given $K$ distributions (or arms) that take value in $[0,1]$, and given a fixed number of samples $T>0$ (or budget) that can be collected sequentially and adaptively from the distributions, the problem of the learner in this setting is to identify the set of distributions with the highest mean

settings.name_in_paper: K Bernoulli bandit problems obtained by flipping arms (technical formulation, lower bound)
unmapped: Learner knows the problem is one of K fully specified Bernoulli problems G^1..G^K with means p_k in [1/4,1/2), p_1=1/2, arm i flipped to 1-p_i in problem i
settings.definition_quote: This is a lower bound that will hold in the much easier (for the learner) problem where the learner knows that the bandit setting it is facing is one of only $K$ given bandit settings (and where it has all information about these settings).

bound.expression_latex: \sup_{\mathcal G \in \mathbb B(a)} \mathbb P_{\mathcal G^{\otimes T}} (\hat k_T \not \in \mathcal A^*(\mathcal G)) \geq \frac{1}{6}\exp\Big(-120\frac{T}{a} \Big)

symbols.a: upper bound on the complexity H defining the class B_a

conditions: sup over all problems with distributions in [0,1] and H <= a

source.label: thm:main3
source.quote: If $T\geq a^2 \big(4\log(6TK)\big)/ (60)^2$, for any bandit strategy that returns arm $\hat k_T$ at time $T$, it holds that $$\sup_{\mathcal G \in \mathbb B(a)} \mathbb P_{\mathcal G^{\otimes T}} (\hat k_T \not \in \mathcal A^*(\mathcal G)) \geq \frac{1}{6}\exp\Big(-120\frac{T}{a} \Big).$$

results.notes: Probability of misidentification; holds even if learner knows a.

bound.expression_latex: \sup_{\mathcal G \in \mathbb B(a)} \Bigg[\mathbb P_{\mathcal G^{\otimes T}} (\hat k_T \not \in \mathcal A^*(\mathcal G)) \times \exp\Big(400\frac{T}{\log(K)H(\mathcal G)} \Big)\Bigg]\geq  \frac{1}{6}

symbols.a: upper bound on the complexity H defining the class B_a

conditions: holds for at least one problem G in B_a, with H_1 = H(G)

source.label: thm:main3
source.quote: If in addition $a \geq 11K^2$ and if $K \geq 2$, then for any bandit strategy that returns arm $\hat k_T$ at time $T$, it holds that $$\sup_{\mathcal G \in \mathbb B(a)} \Bigg[\mathbb P_{\mathcal G^{\otimes T}} (\hat k_T \not \in \mathcal A^*(\mathcal G)) \times \exp\Big(400\frac{T}{\log(K)H(\mathcal G)} \Big)\Bigg]\geq  \frac{1}{6}.$$

results.notes: Normalized sup: there exists a problem G with error probability >= (1/6)exp(-400T/(log(K)H(G))). H_1 is the complexity H of that problem.

symbols.H_max: H(1) = max_i H(i), largest complexity among the K constructed problems

conditions: max over the K constructed Bernoulli problems, any p_2..p_K in [1/4,1/2)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For any bandit strategy that returns the arm $\hat k_T$ at time $T$, it holds that $$\max_{1 \leq i \leq K} \mathbb P_{i} (\hat k_T \neq i) \geq  \frac{1}{6}\exp\Big(-60\frac{T}{H(1)} -2 \ \sqrt[]{T\log(6TK)}\Big),$$

symbols.H_i: complexity H(i) of bandit problem i

conditions: holds for at least one of the K constructed Bernoulli problems i

source.label: thm:main2
source.quote: Assume that $T\geq \max\Big(H(1), H(i)h^*\Big)^2 4\log(6TK)/ (60)^2$.  For any bandit strategy that returns the arm $\hat k_T$ at time $T$, it holds that $$\max_{1 \leq i \leq K} \mathbb P_{i} (\hat k_T \neq i) \geq  \frac{1}{6}\exp\Big(-120\frac{T}{H(1)} \Big)$$

symbols.H_i: complexity H(i) of bandit problem i

conditions: holds for at least one of the K constructed problems

source.label: thm:main2
source.quote: and also $$\max_{1 \leq i \leq K}\Bigg[ \mathbb P_{i} (\hat k_T \neq i) \times \exp\Big(120\frac{T}{{H(i)}h^*} \Big) \Bigg]\geq 1/6.$$
